Tidy CharacteristicFeatures() output for plotting

Source: R/utils-characterize.r
enriched_features.Rd

Turns the output of CharacteristicFeatures() into a per-cluster list of compact tables (term / pvalue / Count) ready for plot_pathways(). For each cluster it keeps the characteristic features that pass a significance cut and, by default, only those that are enriched in the cluster (more frequent among its objects than in the remaining objects) rather than depleted. Empty clusters are dropped.

Usage

enriched_features(
  char,
  data,
  source = 1,
  method = 1,
  sign = 0.05,
  enriched_only = TRUE,
  clean_names = TRUE
)

Arguments

char

Output of CharacteristicFeatures().

data

The binary data matrix whose features were tested (objects in rows, features in columns) - e.g. the target matrix. Used to set the enrichment direction and the per-cluster feature counts.

source

Which tested data source to use within each cluster, by name (e.g. "Target") or index. Default: the first source.

method

Which clustering result in char to use, by name or index. Default 1.

sign

Keep features with adjusted p-value below this. Default 0.05.

enriched_only

If TRUE (default) keep only features more frequent in the cluster than in the rest of the objects; if FALSE keep every significant characteristic feature (enriched or depleted).

clean_names

If TRUE (default) tidy the feature names for display - reversing the make.names() mangling common in binary descriptor matrices (drop a leading X before a digit, turn ./_ runs into spaces), e.g. "X3.oxo.5.alpha_steroid" becomes "3 oxo 5 alpha steroid". Set FALSE to keep the raw column names.

Value

A named list - one element per non-empty cluster - of data frames with columns term, pvalue (adjusted p-value) and Count (number of the cluster's objects carrying the feature), suitable for plot_pathways().

See also

CharacteristicFeatures(), plot_pathways()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
Char <- CharacteristicFeatures(List = list(Weighted = sol),
                               binData = list(Target = targetMat),
                               datanames = "Target", nrclusters = 4)
tabs <- enriched_features(Char, targetMat)
plot_pathways(tabs, style = "circular")
} # }
